questions.explain: Four layers: client (streaming UI, quota display, version navigation, feedback), application (stateless orchestration: gateway, chat orchestrator, agent runtime, text-to-SQL), data (SQL Server at the center — RLS and guardrails enforced here), pipeline (ingestion, eval, drift, anomaly, backup/erasure jobs).
options: Client, application (stateless orchestration), data (SQL Server center), and pipeline layers — cross-cutting concerns live in the database
questions.q: What are the four architecture layers?

questions.explain: Nine stages: 1) gateway auth/rate/tenant, 2) session + message insert, 3) semantic cache check, 4) memory assembly, 5) retrieval with RLS, 6) prompt construction, 7) LLM/agent generation with streaming, 8) output validation + audit, 9) memory update — typically 1–3 seconds, first token under a second.
options: Rate check → session → cache → memory → retrieval → prompt → generation → audit → memory update
The chat turn has no defined stages
questions.q: What are the nine stages of a chat turn?

questions.explain: Daily: ops dashboard, anomaly alerts, dead letters, eval trends. Weekly: profiling refresh, index maintenance, retention sweeps, cache review. Monthly: ledger close, margin analysis, golden-set review, access review. Quarterly: schema exposure, load tests, DR drill, model/pricing updates.
options: Daily dashboards and alerts; weekly maintenance; monthly ledger and margins; quarterly reviews and drills; one incident runbook
questions.q: What is the operational runbook cadence?

questions.explain: Phase 1: chat that works (schema, pooling, sessions, history, audit, basic RAG). Phase 2: multi-tenant production (RLS, quotas, ledger, observability, caching, streaming). Phase 3: intelligence (memory, eval, agents, text-to-SQL). Phase 4: hardening (injection defense, erasure, versioning, multi-agent, scale-out, testing).
options: Phase 1: working chat → Phase 2: multi-tenant production → Phase 3: intelligence → Phase 4: hardening
questions.q: What is the recommended build order for a new team?

questions.explain: The God Prompt (one giant prompt instead of the memory architecture), app-layer RLS (one missed WHERE clause is a breach), unbounded agents (no budgets/approvals — the invoice surprises), embeddings without provenance, and audit as an afterthought.
options: God Prompt, application-layer RLS, unbounded agents, embeddings without provenance, and audit as an afterthought
